PullRequest.Title: standardize provider attribution on AH session telemetry
PullRequest.Body:

## Overview

### What

Identify the agent implementation associated with chat activity using `provider`: for example, `copilotcli`, `claude`, or `codex`. Local and remote sessions using the same implementation have the same provider, independently of the selected language model.

Adds attribution to workbench session invocation/opening, model-picker lifecycle and configuration changes, custom-agent mode changes, handoffs, instruction collection, and response code-block presentation/copy/insert actions. Workbench attribution reads the registered session contribution's `agentHostProviderId`, preserving hyphenated provider IDs and custom session types. Missing expected attribution is `unknown`; known non-Agent Host sessions and non-agent edit sources omit the field.

Edit-survival detail events replace their top-level `harness` field with `provider`, including the existing GitHub mirror. Internal source metadata, source keys, and protocol markers retain `harness`.

Also fixes `agentHost.instructionsCollected`: it now reads provider from the owning session, not the current chat resource scheme. A Copilot peer conversation whose resource is `ahp-chat://...` therefore reports `copilotcli`, not `ahp-chat`.

### Why

Tracked by the cross-cutting AH-filter item in [microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9096](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/9096), alongside [microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9127](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/9127). Consistent attribution reduces event-specific query logic and allows the metrics consumer to classify eligible Copilot AH edit reports as CopilotSDK instead of leaving them in N/A.

## Attribution contract

| Surface | Source of `provider` |
|---|---|
| Workbench invocation/opening, mode changes, handoffs, instruction collection | Registered session contribution's `agentHostProviderId` |
| Model-picker open/change/configuration/close | Registered provider captured at picker open |
| Response code-block presentation/copy/insert | Registered provider of the originating response session |
| Edit-survival details | Provider retained in the originating edit's source attribution |
| Host-native `agentHost.instructionsCollected` | Owning backend session's provider, not the conversation URI scheme |

Code-block `codeSuggested` means response text was presented; `codeAccepted` includes copying or inserting that text. These do not establish an Agent Host file-edit accept/reject workflow. `editTelemetry.codeRejected` and the traditional edit-hunk classes are unchanged by this PR; their additional constructor plumbing has been removed.

`copilotSDK/` events retain their namespace as the discriminator. Generic Git/workbench, install/authentication, and provider-agnostic events are not enriched. No `executionHost` field is introduced. This is not a claim that every existing telemetry event has provider attribution.

## Classification and remote privacy

Adds missing `isMeasurement: true` metadata to existing numeric/Boolean fields on touched events: invocation timings, citation/code-block counts, participant-detection flags, workspace/harness-setting flags, `isAgentHostSession`, and `isClaudeAgent`. These values serialize into Kusto `Measures`, not string `Properties`; the classification metadata now documents that distinction. The corrections do not add payload fields or change their values.

Workbench provider attribution is read from registered metadata rather than parsed from connection-specific session-type names. Remote invocation rows collapse connection-specific `sessionType` and `agent` values to `remote-agent-host`. Invocation and code-block telemetry use the existing authority-free session-ID projection. Tests cover a hyphenated canonical provider and check that the private remote hostname is absent from the invocation payload.

## Rollout and query compatibility

**Deploy [metrics compatibility draft 788309](https://dev.azure.com/devdiv/InternalTools/_git/VSCode_Copilot_Metrics/pullrequest/788309) before shipping the edit-field rename.** Consumers must read nonempty `provider` first and fall back to historical `harness` only when provider is absent/empty. Explicit `unknown` must not fall back to an older attribution. The companion also places historical `origin=agentHost, harness=copilotcli` edit reports in CopilotSDK.

This PR does not publish a live metric set or backfill telemetry. Provider segmentation does not repair statistics whose numerators and denominators use differently attributable Git/session/turn events. A regenerated scorecard still needs to verify meaningful CopilotSDK denominators for edit-only commit/focus measures with both historical and new schemas.

## How to test

Latest code follow-up (`2589c50fc90`):

```powershell
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgentSession.test.ts --grep "instructionsCollected telemetry"
```

**Passed: 5 tests**, including owning-session and peer-chat provider attribution.

```powershell
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\editTelemetry\test\browser\editTelemetry.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\actions\chatCodeblockActions.test.ts
```

**Passed: 25 tests**, preserving code-block actions and edit telemetry after removing rejection-specific additions. `npm run typecheck-client` and `npm run transpile-client` also passed on this revision.

Browser CI-fixture follow-up (`31d27fb0958`, before the scope reduction):

```powershell
npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser webkit --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentSessionsControl.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/promptSyntax/service/promptsService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts --sequential
```

**Passed: 667 tests.** An isolated Electron run covering the reported CI failures passed 136 tests. The broader local Electron run had 11 additional rendering geometry/timing failures; these are not claimed as passing or fixed by this PR.

Live metric publication and regenerated-scorecard validation have not been performed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Completing a chat request and emitting provider-invocation/instruction telemetry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The response and instruction collection already complete before their existing telemetry calls. The diff adds one synchronous provider lookup immediately before logging; it does not delay model invocation, instruction file discovery, or response progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover and parse instruction files during automatic instruction collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing collection over the instruction files applicable to one request; cardinality is unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same instruction discovery and parsing ran before provider attribution was added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These reads remain on the pre-existing instruction-collection critical path; provider resolution occurs only after collection completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit the existing instructionsCollected and interactiveSessionProviderInvoked telemetry events through publicLog2.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing event per collection/request completion; the diff adds one short provider field without adding events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same events were emitted with the same cadence but without provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous event object preparation remains bounded; downstream telemetry transport was already reached.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One lookup and one additional scalar property per completed request or instruction-collection event, independent of request text, instruction-file count, and response size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new concurrency. Each event follows the existing request completion or collection sequence; no loop schedules boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider metadata is read from the already-populated contribution map. There is no cold fetch, miss retry, negative cache, or new cache lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call paths and map-backed provider lookup are directly visible, and no added asynchronous boundary is reachable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact telemetry transport cost varies by appender, but call count is unchanged and payload growth is a bounded provider string.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added constant-sized field and map lookup do not materially change latency, throughput, memory, or I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering completed chat responses with code blocks and copying/inserting code
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Final response rendering already parses markdown and emits one codeSuggested event per code block. The diff adds provider resolution while initializing each block. Copy/insert actions already perform clipboard/editor work before one existing acceptance event; provider lookup is bounded and in-memory.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit the existing editTelemetry.codeSuggested event for each completed code block.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pre-existing telemetry event per code block; the diff adds a scalar provider value to each event but does not increase event count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Suggestion IDs and telemetry were already created for every finalized code block.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Event creation is on final rendering as before. Added provider resolution is local and bounded.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write copied code to the clipboard or apply text/editor changes for insert actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One clipboard or editor operation per explicit action, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same clipboard/editor operation occurred before provider attribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These pre-existing operations dominate the action critical path; provider resolution occurs only for the existing telemetry record.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Final initialization scales with the number of code blocks in one completed response. Each block adds one map lookup, availability check, and small resolved-contribution allocation; action paths add one lookup per explicit user action.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering is synchronous on the UI path but provider lookup performs no I/O and schedules no work. User actions remain serialized by their existing awaits and editor operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Contribution storage is a warm in-memory Map. No cache miss triggers activation or remote discovery; unavailable or absent contributions return immediately.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: initialization is guarded to run once after response completion, contribution lookup is Map-backed, and no new boundary is invoked.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Responses can contain many code blocks, but provider resolution is local and small relative to existing markdown parsing, editor construction, UUID generation, and one telemetry event per block.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression. Although the lookup is repeated per finalized code block, it is bounded local work and does not establish meaningful jank or allocation pressure.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening model/mode pickers, changing configuration, opening sessions, and clicking handoffs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each explicit UI interaction performs one provider lookup before the already-existing telemetry emission. Picker provider is captured once when the telemetry session opens and reused for change/close events.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit existing model-picker, mode-change, handoff, and session-open telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event per corresponding user interaction; unchanged event count, with one added provider field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These interactions emitted the same events without provider attribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing synchronous telemetry submission remains on the interaction path; the diff only adds bounded metadata preparation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One lookup per picker open, mode change, handoff, or session open; independent of model list size and session-history size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new parallelism, queue, limiter, or burst. These are discrete user interactions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider comes from the contribution map; no provider activation, network fetch, or persistent cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all changed callers invoke the same local helper once and retain no additional long-lived collection.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Appender implementation and device speed vary, but there is no multiplicative input or extra boundary call.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The work is constant per user action and picker sessions reuse the captured provider.

Scenarios.Scenario: Flushing edit-survival attribution and host-native instruction telemetry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing edit-window/session flushes prepare detail rows and send telemetry; the diff renames harness to provider and applies a constant unknown fallback. Host-native instruction logging changes which already-held URI supplies the scheme.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send existing edit-source detail telemetry and its existing GitHub mirror.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing event per prepared source row, with the same top-row limits and mirror count; only the field name/value fallback changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same detail events and mirror calls were sent with harness instead of provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialization/transport remains part of the existing flush path; no additional event or payload collection is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit the existing agentHost.instructionsCollected telemetry event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event on the existing instruction-source collection path; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The event already read a URI scheme and emitted the same payload shape.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the URI object supplying the provider scheme changes; event count and timing are unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One scalar field transformation per existing detail row and one property read per host instruction event. Detail-row caps and flush cadence are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new tasks or concurrent boundary calls. Existing flush ordering and telemetry mirror behavior remain unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is added or bypassed; values are read from already-retained attribution/session metadata.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed lines are scalar renames/property reads and existing tests confirm unchanged event cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of edit detail rows varies by tracked sources, but the diff neither raises row limits nor adds per-row boundary calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. Serialization size and work remain effectively constant, with no retention or cleanup lifecycle change.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 38 changed files and every diff page for performance mechanisms. Provider attribution uses an in-memory Map-backed contribution lookup, adds constant-sized telemetry metadata, and does not add expensive boundaries or increase event cardinality. The only collection-scaled lookup is once per finalized code block on an already per-block telemetry path; it is bounded and too small to establish a concrete user-visible regression. No performance finding or regression-fix record is warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
